R101.note: Allowlist of scalar status/type/priority keeps ownerId and operators out of the filter, but any other extra criterion the original honoured (e.g. total, or a nested $in on status) is now silently dropped rather than rejected, so the lookup returns an order the caller's criteria should have excluded; stated, but it is a new restriction on the documented narrowing feature.

R102.note: path.resolve plus path.relative containment before require closes traversal on POSIX and the 400 only fires for escaping names; the check omits path.isAbsolute(relative), which leaves a cross-drive absolute path unblocked on Windows only.

R103.note: HttpPost plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is the right shape, but the existing confirmation page's GET link stops working until the view is rewritten as a token-bearing POST form; the write-up states that as a required follow-up without supplying it.

R104.note: Moving param into filterArgs with {0}/{1} lets JNDI's SearchFilter escape *, (, ), backslash and NUL; only visible side effect is the not-found message now prints the {0} template instead of the searched value.

R105.note: Single snprintf into the 64-byte buffer with a >= sizeof check rejects exactly the inputs that previously overflowed and leaves fitting inputs producing the identical AUDIT user:action output and return 0.

R106.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param('s')/execute/get_result is the correct parameterised shape and preserves the null-on-failure and first-row semantics.

R107.note: Set.of allowlist in the service keeps ${sort} to four column names and preserves tenantId binding, but any unrecognised value (including a direction suffix like 'status DESC') is silently coerced to created_at rather than rejected, so a caller gets differently ordered rows with no signal; stated, but a silent fallback.

R108.note: Extension now derived from the file-type detected MIME via a fixed map, so a client-supplied .php extension never reaches disk; the stored id's extension may differ from the upload name (.jpeg becomes .jpg), which the write-up states and which blocks nothing.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES and UTF-8 on both values at the concatenation point is the right sink-side encoding for element content; only edge is that omitting ENT_SUBSTITUTE returns an empty string for invalid UTF-8 input.

R110.note: Early return when channelIndex >= calibrationTable.size() is the correct guard for a std::array subscript and changes nothing for in-range updates.

R111.note: Reproduced with a stubbed smtplib.SMTP in a scratch dir: sendmail's quoteaddr passes unparseable input through verbatim, so a sender of a@b.com> AUTH=<x@y.com is sent as 'mail from:<a@b.com> AUTH=<x@y.com>' (ESMTP parameter injection survives) and CRLF is stopped only by putcmd's own newline check, which the original docmd path already hit - the switch adds no neutralisation of the address itself; it also changes behaviour unstated, raising SMTPSenderRefused/SMTPRecipientsRefused on non-250 replies where the original returned OK regardless.

R112.note: id = ANY($1::int[]) with ids passed as a bound parameter is the idiomatic node-postgres replacement for a hand-built IN list and preserves selection by id; the ::int[] cast assumes an int4 id column (an untyped ANY($1) would have avoided that assumption) and an empty array now returns no rows instead of a syntax error.

R113.note: pathinfo PATHINFO_EXTENSION on the final extension with a strict in_array closes the double-extension bypass, but the file is also renamed to a sha256 hash, discarding the original filename the case comments document as intentionally preserved for the uploads listing and changing the returned path; stated, but beyond what the fix needed.

R114.note: resize(count) makes the packet[i] write in-bounds, but the same statement still reads fields[i] unchecked, so a count larger than fields.size() remains an out-of-bounds access instead of being rejected or reported as the contract requires; nothing else observable changes for valid counts.

R115.note: PreAuthorize on processMonthEndCleanup is enforced through the proxy on the controller's call, which is the correct place to close the self-invocation gap; whichever identity drives the nightly job must now hold ADMIN, consistent with the ADMIN requirement already on deleteInvoice but not called out in the write-up.

R116.note: Arrow-function callback capturing reminderId and message removes string evaluation entirely and records the same log entry the original intended.

R117.note: res.sendFile(requestedFile, { root: reportsDir }) hands containment to send's own up-path check, which the original defeated by pre-joining the path; legitimate relative names resolve to the same file as before.
